claims.title: Company positioning
claims.statement: MATTER POISE is a newly established U.S. AI-driven hardware R&D and manufacturing company based in Georgia, U.S., as confirmed by management. It connects self-developed actuation, engineering services, production supply and planned software workflows. The team confirms info@matterpoise.com as its contact address.
claims.qualification: The company stage, location and contact are management-confirmed. Investors can request formation records, ownership information and the legal contracting entity for documentary diligence.

claims.title: Hardware portfolio
claims.statement: The portfolio includes micro drives, larger joint modules, FlatHill dexterous manipulation end-effectors, GROUNDWISE mobile systems, WAYROUND spherical systems and a separate Matter Poise dual-arm integration platform. Management describes the arm, spherical and quadruped platforms as applications of shared large-joint modules and a common hardware architecture. Reusing this engineering base is intended to limit duplicated development and support a broader set of customer applications.
claims.qualification: Shared architecture does not mean identical platform BOMs or a measured reuse percentage. Each platform still needs its own integration, controls, testing and validation; readiness varies by SKU. The expected R&D efficiency has not been quantified in the public brief.

claims.title: Self-developed joint architecture
claims.statement: Micro families: M01 / M01 Neo / M02. Larger-joint families: WZ53 / WZ79 / WZ119. Management reports established joint-module engineering capability supported by completed technical drawings. Modules are currently predominantly manufactured in China and imported into the U.S.; the company plans to establish U.S. joint-module production lines gradually.
claims.qualification: The drawings and current manufacturing model are management-reported. Self-developed architecture does not mean every chip, motor or input is fabricated internally. Revision-specific performance, manufacturing readiness, rights and transfer milestones remain subjects for documentary review.

claims.title: Manufacturing experience
claims.statement: Team materials report 150+ robot deliveries in prior career programs, with experience in mechanisms, embedded control, supplier coordination, production transfer and field delivery.
claims.qualification: These are not MATTER POISE shipments, current customer orders or audited company traction. Prior program responsibility and delivery references should be verified. No individual names are included in this public brief.

claims.title: Industry order data
claims.statement: A3 reported 36,766 North American robot orders worth $2.25B in calendar 2025. H1 2026 totals were 17,995 units and $1.166B. Non-automotive customers represented 56% of Q2 2026 units.
claims.qualification: Complete-robot order data, not a U.S.-only market or MATTER POISE component TAM. Do not add overlapping or different reporting periods. A3 publication dates: 6 Feb and 11 Aug 2026.

claims.title: Customers and first sale
claims.status: Management-confirmed company stage and commercial strategy
claims.statement: MATTER POISE is newly established and currently has no orders, as confirmed by management on 14 October 2026. Initial target customers are U.S. robotics OEMs, applied-AI / research teams and automation integrators. The planned path is evaluation hardware, scoped engineering and pilot lots, followed by scheduled component or assembly supply.
claims.qualification: Target segments and sales stages describe the commercial plan, not current booked business. No orders does not itself establish revenue status or whether evaluation conversations exist; those should be confirmed separately with the team.

claims.title: Repeatable revenue model
claims.statement: The website models 5 programs × 500 robots per program per year × 12 modules per robot × $250 selling price = $7.5M annual component revenue and 30,000 module shipments.
claims.qualification: All inputs are hypothetical. This is not current revenue, a forecast, signed pipeline, TAM or investment return. Selling price is distinct from component budget; gross margin is not established.

claims.title: Joint and dog component inputs
claims.statement: Large joint modules are budgeted at ~$150–500 each; micro drives at ~$100 each. Dog CNC structures are ~$800 and motion-control hardware ~$500.
claims.qualification: These are budget inputs, not supplier commitments, audited production cost or customer quotes. Controls exclude Jetson compute and drives already integrated in joint modules.

claims.title: Default system budgets
claims.statement: Quadruped: ~$5.2k–$10.7k; dexterous hand: ~$2.5k–$3.2k; spherical robot: ~$6.9k–$10.2k; dual-arm platform: ~$10.1k–$18.2k.
claims.qualification: Dog assumes 12 leg joints plus four separately budgeted wheel drives and Orin NX 16GB. Hand assumes 20 micro drives and excludes external host compute. Sphere assumes an AGX Orin 64GB developer kit. Dual arms assume 14 arm joints plus two 20-drive hands. Quantities and unquoted line items are assumptions; DOF alone does not establish actuator count.

claims.title: Budget boundary
claims.statement: The model totals non-overlapping component lines. Shares are each line midpoint divided by the total midpoint; displayed figures are rounded.
claims.qualification: Excludes end-product assembly, test labor, yield loss, freight, duty, tax, software, warranty and operating expense. It is not a landed COGS or retail price. Recalculate before proposing margin or savings.

claims.title: NVIDIA compute
claims.statement: NVIDIA FAQ checked 12 Oct 2026: Orin Nano Super developer kit $399; AGX Orin developer kit $3,499; Orin NX 16GB module $999; AGX Orin 64GB module $2,999. Production-module prices are suggested 1,000+ unit figures.
claims.qualification: Refresh pricing and availability for current procurement. Developer kits are for development; production uses an appropriate module and carrier / thermal design. No NVIDIA partnership is asserted.

claims.title: U.S. sourcing and origin
claims.statement: U.S. supplier purchasing share and U.S.-qualifying component cost are separate measures. NVIDIA lists U.S.-origin SKUs for Orin NX 16GB (900-13767-0000-0A1) and AGX Orin 64GB (900-13701-0050-0A0).
claims.qualification: Brand nationality and a U.S. invoice do not prove the purchased lot’s origin. Allocation, actual price and declarations must be confirmed. No actual domestic-content percentage is established by the public BOM.

claims.title: FCC and domestic content
claims.statement: The published source set includes FCC DA 26-786 and the referenced domestic-end-product rules. The general FAR test requires U.S. manufacture and domestic component cost exceeding 65% through 2028, then exceeding 75% from 2029, with applicable exceptions.
claims.qualification: Check current primary rules and the finished SKU. Fixed industrial arms and mobile platforms can have different scope. Normal equipment authorization is separate. No MATTER POISE FCC approval, legal eligibility determination or unconditional Made in USA claim is established. Do not infer permanent chip exemptions; FTC origin claims have a separate standard.

claims.title: IP and freedom to operate
claims.status: Management-reported technical assets and planned IP placement
claims.statement: Management reports completed joint-module technical drawings and relevant joint-module patent/IP assets being prepared for placement in the U.S. company. Completing that placement before the pre-A financing round is the stated target. This planned consolidation is intended to support the U.S. company’s long-term engineering and manufacturing position.
claims.qualification: The pre-A milestone is a target, not a completed transfer or registration. This brief does not specify patent grant status, patent numbers, ownership-transfer mechanisms or completed product-specific FTO. Request the asset schedule, current ownership and filing status, executed documentation when available, and appropriate FTO analysis. Ownership and freedom to operate are separate questions.

claims.title: ROSE software
claims.statement: ROSE is proprietary AI-assisted engineering software in development. Its proposed workflows connect from-scratch-to-demo and demo-to-manufacturing work. Management reports an early prototype; the investor roadmap places commercialization in a post-2027 stage, subject to validation.
claims.qualification: The public workflow is an explainer, not a working software demo or verified shipped capability. No current ARR, paid subscriptions, measured engineering productivity gain or committed launch date is established.

claims.title: Manufacturing and RSI
claims.status: Current manufacturing model and staged roadmap
claims.statement: Current joint-module supply is predominantly based on manufacturing in China and import into the U.S. The company plans a gradual build-out of U.S. joint-module production lines, supported by engineering documentation and process transfer. Dedicated assembly, calibration and test processes are intended to precede greater automation of stable tasks. The long-term RSI direction is evidence-based process improvement with engineering review, traceability and rollback.
claims.qualification: Planned U.S. production lines and lights-out capabilities are future milestones, not present installed capacity. Timing and scale depend on demand, funding, process qualification, yield and good-unit economics; the public brief commits to no completed factory or guaranteed cost reduction.

claims.title: Fundraising
claims.statement: Management confirms an approximately $8–10M seed fundraising planning range as of 14 October 2026. The illustrative $10M case allocates about $2M to equipment, $3M to team and operations, $3M to R&D, materials and transfer, and $2M to working capital and contingency.
claims.qualification: This is a plan, not money already raised or confirmed round terms. The final amount, valuation, runway, cap table, commitments and allocation require current team confirmation.

claims.title: Demonstrations
claims.statement: Company-published materials include prototype demonstrations and simulation footage. The corporate website also offers edited GROUNDWISE, FlatHill and English-language WAYROUND inspection demonstrations. Investor exploded views are AI-assisted conceptual illustrations; official NVIDIA references are external context.
claims.qualification: Clips are qualitative, not independent performance, safety or reliability validation. Editing and translation do not add validation. Simulation is not real-world operation. External references are not customer, partnership or endorsement evidence.
